subject: Physics
title: Average Speed vs Average Velocity
summary: Walk 4 km to school and back in an hour: average speed 4 km/h, average velocity zero. One uses total distance, the other displacement.
keyPoints: A round trip has average velocity **0** but a non-zero average speed.
Never average two speeds directly: 4 and 12 km/h over equal distances give **6**, not 8.

blocks.p: A boy walks 2 km to school and 2 km back in **1 hour**. Distance = 4 km, so average speed = **4 km/h**. He ends where he started, so displacement = 0 and average velocity = **0**.

blocks.alt: Home to school and back: two trails of 2 km, displacement zero
blocks.caption: Distance 4 km, displacement 0.

blocks.formula: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time;  average velocity = total displacement ÷ total time

blocks.p: Going 12 km at 4 km/h takes 3 h; returning 12 km at 12 km/h takes 1 h. Average speed = 24 km ÷ 4 h = **6 km/h**, not (4 + 12) ÷ 2 = 8, because more time is spent on the slow leg.

blocks.alt: Time bars: 3 hours at 4 km/h and 1 hour at 12 km/h
blocks.caption: The slow leg takes 3 times longer.

quiz.q: A car goes 60 km east in 1 h and 40 km west in 1 h. Its average speed is:
For the same car, the average velocity is:
quiz.explain: Displacement = 60 − 40 = 20 km east in 2 h = 10 km/h east.

quiz.q: A runner finishes one full lap of a circular track. Average velocity for the lap is:
quiz.explain: Start and end are the same point, so displacement and average velocity are zero.

quiz.q: 12 km at 4 km/h, then 12 km back at 12 km/h. Average speed?
quiz.explain: Times 3 h + 1 h = 4 h; 24 km ÷ 4 h = 6 km/h.
Displacement is never longer than the path, so |average velocity| ≤ average speed.

simulation.reason: Choosing a straight, there-and-back, zig-zag or circular path and comparing the average-speed and average-velocity readouts is exactly this topic; the existing Speed vs Velocity simulation already computes both, so it is reused.
simulation.objective: Compare average speed (path length ÷ time) with average velocity (displacement ÷ time) on different paths.
instructions: Pick a path: straight, there-and-back, zig-zag or circle.
Press Play or drag the time slider to the end.
Read the average speed and the average velocity.
On there-and-back and the full circle, see the average velocity fall to zero while the average speed does not.
